messages:
maya: saw a spike in 5xxs + routing errors, alarm fired for smart-routing fallback loops. p95 token latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s. Alerts: 503 / 504 / backend timeout. paging devon (on-call). :rotating_light:
pagerbot: Incident created INC-2026-045 by alert-manager at 2026-07-12 09:12UTC — paging: @devon.
devon: on it, grabbing logs now. initial hypothesis: client retries + automatic region fallback are doubling traffic into EU pool causing thundering herd.
samir: confirming — seen doubled RPS to eu-west-2 model-variant:babbage-v2-quant, concurrent inflight up 2.1x. KV cache misses spiked during failovers.
maya: is fallback policy set to route to any compatible variant? I think the policy allows cross-region fallback + variant downgrade.
ken: yep, policy: `fallback: { allow_region_fallback: true, prefer_compatible: true }` — that combinatoric rule is risky with client retry backoff.
devon: mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily disable cross-region fallback for affected customers, 2) apply short rate-limit on retries at the edge, 3) scale up EU pool if needed.
ryan: +1 for disabling cross-region fallback — quick step: patch routing config, rollout to 10% then 100% — we need the command.
samir: paste of current routing snippet:
```
routes:
  - match: {region: eu}
    primary: model-variant:babbage-v2-quant
    fallback:
      - model-variant:babbage-v2-quant-rt
      - region: us-east
      - model-variant: gpt-compact
```

ken: change to remove region fallback and prefer local variants only, temp patch:
```
routes[0].fallback = ["model-variant:babbage-v2-quant-rt", "model-variant:gpt-compact"]
```
apply via `rctl apply routing --patch --scope incidents`
maya: devon, can you gate the patch to the tenant group causing the spike first (they're tied to customer IDs A12, B34)? we want to avoid global fallout.
devon: doing canary to affected tenant list now. running: `rctl rollout routing --canary customers=A12,B34 --wait 60s`
incidents-bot: rollout started: routing-config patch id rc-5579, canary customers A12,B34.
samir: metric note — client retry rate for those customers increased 4x in the last 6m. exponential backoff not working because clients are capping backoff at 2s.
ryan: ops ask: any chance we can push a small response header instructing longer retry-after? maybe shorter-term mitigation if clients respect it.
ken: we can add `Retry-After: 10` on 503s from the router for those tenant prefixes. quick patch to edge.
maya: customer-success, can you start drafting comms? affected customers might notice increased latency/errors for the last ~30m.
customer-success: drafting now. early message will say: "We're investigating transient errors for requests routed to EU variants; mitigation in progress."
devon: canary patch succeeded for A12,B34. traffic normalized for them within ~45s, inflight dropped ~60%. starting broader rollout to all EU tenants.
incidents-bot: rollout rc-5579 progressed: canary OK -> 50% -> 100% (estimated completion in 90s).
samir: after 100% rollout, overall RPS to eu pool dropped from 18k to 8.6k — still elevated vs baseline but stable. retry amplification reduced by ~58%.
ryan: scaling note: we also spun up 6 additional gpu workers in eu for 10m just in case — cost impact tracked in incident.
ken: follow-up: need to update fallback policy to detect high-retry amplification and avoid region fallback automatically. adding a guard: if downstream retry-rate > X then disable region fallback for that route.
maya: agree, propose rule: `fallback_guard: { max_retry_amplification: 1.3, window_seconds: 120 }` — start conservative.
devon: will open an RFC and a follow-up ticket to add guard + rollout tests. ticket INF-1182.
customer-success: list of potentially impacted customers assembled: A12, B34, C56, D78. sending proactive notes to A12/B34.
ryan: logs snippet showing amplification pattern:
```
[09:11:23] client req id c-8a -> router eu -> model old -> 504
[09:11:23] client retry c-8a -> router us -> routed to eu via fallback -> model same -> 200 (heavy load)
[09:11:24] more retries -> more fallbacks -> pile-on
```
samir: root cause summary: combination of permissive region fallback + short client retry backoffs created a feedback loop. when eu nodes transiently dropped a few workers, many requests retried and were routed across region and back, causing doubled inflight and cache thrash.
maya: action items captured: 1) patch routing to disable region fallback for now (done), 2) add retry-after header (done), 3) temporary scale-up (done), 4) RFC for fallback_guard (INF-1182), 5) test harness to simulate retry-amplification (devex ticket).
devon: assigning oncall followup: ken to track post-mortem and policy changes, samir to own metric alerts tuning, ryan to own auto-scale rollback window, maya to coordinate customer comms.
ken: will own PM. starting postmortem doc and will post link here when ready.
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared at 09:28UTC.
maya: thanks team. keep monitoring for 2 hours, update if any regressions. :thumbsup:
